summary: The tested changes close public employee-data access, client-approved administrator sessions, unverified legacy-email ownership, self-assigned privilege changes and direct teacher/fund critical writes. The rules compile and are exercised by emulator tests. This is not a full least-privilege or production deployment certification; privileged record access and administrative legacy schemas remain broader than the final target.

findings.issue: Production adoption requires verified Firebase Auth users and canonical server-managed UID profiles. Legacy email-key profiles intentionally stop granting staff access.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile staff identities and assignment data before coordinated rollout, using protected account management and explicit role review.

findings.issue: Verified faculty and several administrator modules retain broad student-document read access. Authorized reports/register/certificate/roll modules retain broad record-editing authority needed by existing workflows.
findings.recommendation: Introduce purpose-specific read projections and field-specific server mutation commands before reducing those shared collection capabilities.

findings.check: The Update Bypass and Type Safety
findings.issue: Canonical user authority fields are immutable to clients, but legacy administrator academic imports and dynamic student/archive maps do not yet have complete field-level schema validation.
findings.recommendation: Move remaining administrative ingestion and nested archive changes to validated backend commands, retaining before-images and explicit per-module authorization.

findings.issue: Uploads and public requests are bounded, but all dynamic administrative document arrays and client-created activity data are not protected by consistent application-specific quotas or retention policies.
findings.recommendation: Enforce per-job row/byte limits and retention in server ingestion and audit endpoints; configure expiry cleanup for ephemeral backend documents.

findings.issue: Emulator checks cover 26 authorization cases and nine backend integrity cases. SMTP, live App Check, deployment headers, legacy account migration and authenticated visual journeys have not been certified in production.
findings.recommendation: Complete the documented coordinated release and real-account acceptance matrix. Keep admissions closed during session rollover until server-wide rollover locking is implemented.
